brief: Goldman's weekly positioning wrap: hedge funds net sold global equities for the first time in 5 weeks, with gross leverage down to 308.0% and net leverage to 77.3%, driven by short and long sales. Seven of 11 sectors were net sold while Info Tech, Financials and Cons Disc were bought. Europe was the only region net bought, led by new longs in Financials at a 6.8 to 1 buy to sell ratio, widening Europe's overweight to 1.61% versus MSCI World while North America stayed underweight at -16.98%. CTAs sold $15bn of equities over the week ($70bn over the month), but the desk's models now predict CTAs turning buyers on a one-week and one-month horizon. Retail signals are mixed: SPX retail imbalance stayed positive every day while equity mutual funds saw $10bn of outflows. GS Sentiment Indicator held at -0.9, its lowest since August 2025, which the desk reads as light positioning. Combined with 85% of the S&P 500 heading into buyback blackout by week's end and seasonally strong October and November buyback months, the desk calls the setup a glass half full one.
